key_features.classic_presentation: Severe constipation presents with LOWER ABDOMINAL cramping pain and BLOATING that is INTERMITTENT (comes and goes) and MILD TO MODERATE severity (3-6/10). Onset is GRADUAL over days to weeks (not acute). Key symptom: NO BOWEL MOVEMENT for 3-7+ days, or hard/pellet-like stools when passing. Pain is RELIEVED by bowel movement or passing gas. Location: Lower abdomen, diffuse cramping. Key associated symptoms: Bloating, sensation of incomplete evacuation, straining, hard stools. Usually NO fever, NO vomiting (unless severe impaction). Key history: Poor fiber/water intake, sedentary lifestyle, medications (opioids, iron, anticholinergics), chronic constipation pattern. Key positives: Gradual onset, able to pass gas (unlike obstruction), pain better after defecation. Key negatives: Sudden onset with inability to pass gas suggests obstruction not constipation. Vomiting is uncommon. Severe pain suggests alternative diagnosis.

red_flags: Sudden onset severe constipation with vomiting - possible bowel obstruction, needs urgent imaging
Complete inability to pass gas - suggests obstruction not simple constipation
Blood in stool with weight loss - concern for colon cancer, needs colonoscopy
New onset constipation in elderly - higher risk of serious pathology
